shots.voiceover: Why are you more productive on a video call than working alone? There's actually a neurological reason.
shots.textOverlay: why you work better when someone else is there

shots.voiceover: You've been putting off a task for three days. You get on a Zoom call, your camera off, other person doing their own work — and you finish in forty minutes.

This is called body doubling — and for ADHD brains, the presence of another person activates the accountability circuit in the prefrontal cortex, which in turn releases enough dopamine to bridge the initiation gap. You're essentially borrowing someone else's focus. Research from ADHD coach pioneers including Dr. Ned Hallowell confirms it — social presence is one of the most reliable ADHD productivity hacks that actually works.
